BOOTH1.name: Dust extraction booth
BOOTH1.detail: Dal Prete IWATER 4 MT water-wall booth, s/n 116-19 (2019)
BOOTH1.recorded: Daily (operator) | Weekly (Mon) | Sludge tank every 10-15 days | Monthly fan blades + bolts
pre_use: Water level at the mark (10 cm below the top edge)
Fans and pump running, curtain flowing evenly
Work INSIDE the booth, facing the water wall
No dust or mist escaping the face
BOOTH1.why: COSHH reg 9(1): the booth must be kept in efficient working order and in a clean condition, checked weekly (L5 para 172) and examined every 14 months. The tank is emptied every 10-15 days because HSE sheet ST3A says contaminated water is replaced per the maker's instructions.

RPE1.name: Powered visor respirator
RPE1.detail: Trend Airshield Pro, EN 12941 TH2P-S, APF 20
RPE1.recorded: Weekly wearer log | Monthly check (CHK-002 Part B) | Filter change log
pre_use: Battery charged, fan running, air felt at the face
Visor clean, no cracks, seal in place
RPE1.why: HSE Prohibition Notice PN-01: no rotary cutting or polishing without a powered mask of APF 20. COSHH reg 9(3): reusable RPE examined monthly (HSG53 para 90) and the record kept 5 years. A flat battery = no protection.

RPE2.recorded: Weekly wearer log (FORM 023 p2) | Monthly check | Filter change log
pre_use: Filter fitted and seated, not loaded
Facepiece and seal clean, no damage
RPE2.why: HSE Prohibition Notice PN-01: no rotary cutting or polishing without a powered mask of APF 20. COSHH reg 9(3): reusable RPE examined monthly (HSG53 para 90) and the record kept 5 years. A flat battery = no protection.

pre_use: Filter fitted and seated, not loaded
Facepiece and seal clean, no damage
RPE3.why: HSE Prohibition Notice PN-01: no rotary cutting or polishing without a powered mask of APF 20. COSHH reg 9(3): reusable RPE examined monthly (HSG53 para 90) and the record kept 5 years. A flat battery = no protection.

TOOL1.name: Wet air cutting saw 125 mm
pre_use: WATER flowing at the blade BEFORE it touches stone
Blade correct, tight, no cracks or missing segments
Air hose, couplings and clips sound
Powered mask (APF 20) + ear defenders ON - 92 dB(A)
Only inside the booth, fan + water running
TOOL1.why: PUWER reg 5/6: work equipment maintained and inspected at suitable intervals, result recorded - HSE sets weekly for heavy industry (HSG107). Water must flow before the blade turns (HSE sheet ST3A, Prohibition Notice PN-01).

SAW1.name: Bridge saw
pre_use: Guards and enclosure in place, nothing bypassed
Water flowing at the blade before cutting
SAW1.why: PUWER reg 5/6: maintained, inspected at suitable intervals, recorded. PUWER reg 11/16: guards and emergency stops kept working - tested monthly (L22 para 89). COSHH reg 9 / HSE sheet ST3A: water and mist control working before every cut.

SAW2.name: Cobalm Ideal saw
SAW2.detail: OUT OF USE - HSE Prohibition Notice PN-02 until guarded
SAW2.recorded: Only: still isolated, tagged out, not used
pre_use: DO NOT USE - HSE PROHIBITION NOTICE in force
SAW2.why: HSE Prohibition Notice PN-02 (3 Sep 2026): this saw may not be used until it is guarded to PUWER reg 11 - a guard-locking interlock that holds the door shut until the blade has stopped, or an enclosure with light curtain and braking - and HSE told.

CNC1.name: CNC workstation
pre_use: Guards, doors and interlocks in place
CNC1.why: PUWER reg 5/6: maintained, inspected at suitable intervals, recorded. PUWER reg 11/16: guards, light curtain and emergency stops kept working - tested monthly (L22 para 89). COSHH reg 9 / ST3A: water suppression working before use.

POL1.name: Edge polisher
POL1.why: PUWER reg 5/6: maintained, inspected at suitable intervals, recorded. PUWER reg 11/16: guards and emergency stops kept working - tested monthly (L22 para 89). COSHH reg 9 / ST3A: water suppression working before use.

AIR1.name: Compressor + 3 air receivers
AIR1.recorded: Weekly: drain receivers, leaks, gauge, safety valve, hoses
pre_use: Compressed air NEVER used for blowing down clothes or dust
AIR1.why: Pressure Systems Safety Regs reg 12: the system properly maintained in good repair to prevent danger; reg 9: examined under Zurich's written scheme ZE/707250. Draining the receivers stops the corrosion that makes a receiver burst.

RACK1.name: Slab storage poles / racks (yard)
RACK1.detail: Vertical slab poles / racks - A-frames no longer used
pre_use: Slabs restrained, leaning IN, nothing overhanging
Poles / posts upright, base and floor fixings sound
Fall zone clear, forklift route clear
Load / max slab count notice visible
RACK1.why: PUWER reg 5/6: racking is work equipment - inspected at suitable intervals and recorded. HSE HSG76 para 645: weekly inspection with a written record; para 646: competent inspection every 12 months. A tipping slab is the sector's classic fatality.

FIRE-AL.why: Fire Safety Order 2005 art 17: fire equipment kept in efficient working order under a suitable system of maintenance. The government's factories guide and BS 5839-1 set a WEEKLY call-point test. With ear defenders and masks on, the alarm is the only warning.

pre_use: Kit stocked to the contents list
FA1.why: First-Aid Regs 1981 reg 3: adequate and appropriate first-aid equipment. HSE code L74 para 38: contents examined frequently, restocked after use, out-of-date items disposed of. Silica slurry in the eye is our likely injury.

SITE.name: Monthly site walk (CHK-003)
SITE.detail: Whole site - yard, factory, fire, welfare, paperwork
pre_use: Walk the whole site with the form open

SITE.why: Management Regs 1999 reg 5: the employer must monitor and review its health and safety arrangements. This walk is the management check that every other check is happening - and the evidence HSE will ask for by 7 Dec 2026.
